title: A Critical Analysis of a Multi-Input CNN Architecture for Quantum-Enhanced Forecasting
journal_or_venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW)
abstract_summary: The paper evaluates a hybrid quantum-classical pipeline that encodes 1D financial technical indicators (20-day SMA and Bollinger Bands) into 2D images using a simulated Quantum Gramian Angular Field (QGAF) and classifies next-day stock direction with a multi-input CNN. Empirical results on major US equities show the model overfits severely, achieving modest test accuracy (~54.2%) with strong bias toward predicting upward movements. The main contribution is a critical, reproducible baseline and analysis highlighting limitations and directions for future work in quantum-inspired feature engineering for finance.
methodology_description: The study constructs an end-to-end hybrid quantum-inspired feature engineering and deep learning pipeline for daily stock direction classification. Historical daily close prices for selected U.S. equities were used to compute two 20-day technical indicators (20-day Simple Moving Average and the Upper Bollinger Band). The indicator time series were segmented into overlapping 20-day windows; each window was labeled by the next-day price movement (Up=1, Down=0). Each 20-length window was transformed into a 20x20 grayscale image using a Quantum Gramian Angular Field (QGAF) encoding: each time-series value xi was mapped to an angle θi (= xi) used in a single-qubit U3 rotation (U3(θi,0,0)) in a noise-free Qiskit Aer simulation, and the QGAF matrix entries were computed as Qi,j = cos(θi + θj). The SMA and Bollinger Band QGAF images formed two parallel input channels into an identical-branch multi-input CNN. Each branch applied Conv2D (32 filters, 3x3, ReLU) and 2x2 MaxPooling, then flattened; branch outputs were concatenated and passed to a Dense(50, ReLU) and a final Sigmoid output neuron. The model was trained with Adam (lr=0.001) minimizing binary cross-entropy for 300 epochs with batch size 32. Performance was evaluated on a held-out test set using accuracy, confusion matrix, precision, recall, and F1-score.
experimental_setup: QGAF encoding simulated using Qiskit AerSimulator in a noise-free environment. CNN implemented in TensorFlow v2.10. Training performed on a workstation with an NVIDIA RTX 3080 GPU. Model trained for 300 epochs with batch size 32 and Adam optimizer (learning rate 0.001).
dataset_used: Historical daily close prices for selected major U.S. equities (explicitly AAPL and GOOGL) from 2010-01-01 to 2024-01-01, used to compute 20-day Simple Moving Average and Upper Bollinger Band (SMA + 2 * 20-day stddev).
experiment_input: Source: yfinance historical daily data for AAPL and GOOGL (2010-01-01 to 2024-01-01). For each indicator, time series were windowed into overlapping 20-day segments (n=20). Target label: binary next-day movement (price at t+1 > price at t => Up=1, else Down=0). Approximately 15,000 labeled 20-day windows per indicator were produced. Data were randomly shuffled and split into training (70%), validation (15%), and test (15%). Each 20-day window was encoded into a 20x20 grayscale QGAF image; SMA and Bollinger Band produced two channels (processed in parallel branches).
experiment_process: 1) Acquire daily close prices via yfinance. 2) Compute 20-day SMA and Upper Bollinger Band for each day. 3) Create overlapping 20-day windows of each indicator series; label each window by next-day up/down. 4) For each 20-length window X={x1..x20}, map each xi to angle θi = xi; simulate single-qubit U3(θi,0,0) rotations and compute QGAF matrix Qi,j = cos(θi + θj) using Qiskit Aer (noise-free). 5) Produce 20x20 QGAF images for SMA and BB. 6) Feed images into a multi-input CNN: per-branch Conv2D(32,3x3,ReLU) -> MaxPool2D(2x2) -> Flatten. 7) Concatenate branch outputs -> Dense(50,ReLU) -> Output Sigmoid. 8) Compile with Adam (lr=0.001), binary cross-entropy loss. 9) Train for 300 epochs, batch size 32, monitor validation. 10) Evaluate on held-out test set and compute accuracy, confusion matrix, precision, recall, F1.
experiment_output: Primary reported metrics: test accuracy = 54.2%. Confusion matrix for N=1250: True Negative (Down predicted Down) = 54; False Positive (Down actual, Up predicted) = 580; False Negative (Up actual, Down predicted) = 44; True Positive = 572. Class metrics: Down class precision=0.551, recall=0.085, F1=0.147; Up class precision=0.496, recall=0.928, F1=0.646. Baseline comparison: random guess ~50% accuracy (discussed qualitatively). Training/validation curves showed >90% training accuracy and validation ~50-55%, indicating severe overfitting.

hardware_details.simulator: Qiskit AerSimulator (noise-free, used for QGAF encoding)

reproducibility_notes: The paper lists the frameworks and parameter settings (Qiskit v0.44, TensorFlow v2.10, learning rate, epochs, batch size, network architecture) and the data source (yfinance) and date ranges, which enable partial reproduction. However, no code repository or explicit random seed / data split seeds are provided and there is no public release of processed datasets or scripts. The QGAF implementation details (mapping theta_i = xi and Qi,j = cos(xi+xj)) are described, but exact preprocessing/scaling of xi (if any) and other implementation minutiae are not specified. Overall, reproduction is feasible in principle but would require reimplementation and may yield differences without shared code and seeds.

results_summary: The paper implements a simulated quantum-inspired feature pipeline (QGAF) that converts 20-day SMA and Bollinger Upper Band windows into 20x20 images, inputs them into a two-branch multi-input CNN, and evaluates performance on ~15k labeled segments per indicator from two equities (2010–2024). The model fits training data (>90% training accuracy) but fails to generalize (validation ~50–55%), achieving a test accuracy of 54.2%. Confusion-matrix-derived metrics show a strong bias toward predicting 'Up' (Up recall 0.928, precision 0.496) and very poor detection of 'Down' (Down recall 0.085). The authors conclude the approach currently suffers from overfitting and dataset/architecture limitations, present the QGAF pipeline as an empirical baseline, and recommend larger datasets, stronger models, and eventual testing on real quantum hardware.

quantum_advantage_detail: No quantum advantage is demonstrated. The work uses a simulated, noise-free quantum circuit as an encoding/feature-map (QGAF) but provides no evidence that this encoding yields superior predictive performance versus classical encodings; authors explicitly ran the quantum part in simulation and note that execution on real NISQ hardware is future work to assess hardware effects.
limitations: Dataset scale and diversity: dataset (~15,000 segments) generated from only a few equities and likely lacks diversity across sectors and market regimes (author-stated).

Simulated quantum environment: QGAF encoding was performed in a noise-free simulator; results are idealized and may not reflect behavior on real NISQ hardware with gate errors and decoherence (author-stated).
Architectural simplicity: the CNN was intentionally kept simple as a baseline and may be insufficient to extract robust, generalizable features from QGAF images (author-stated).

Overfitting and class bias: the model exhibits severe overfitting (train accuracy >> validation) and a strong bias toward predicting the 'Up' class, failing to detect most 'Down' instances (author-stated).
External validity concerns: uncertain generalization to other asset classes (commodities, forex) or different market regimes (high vs. low volatility) (author-stated).
[inferred] Limited feature set: only two technical indicators (20-day SMA and Bollinger Upper Band) were used, which may omit other informative signals and reduce representational richness.

[inferred] Single-qubit encoding per timepoint: QGAF as implemented maps each timepoint to a single-qubit U3 rotation without multi-qubit entanglement, potentially limiting expressivity of the feature map.

[inferred] Mapping and scaling issues: the paper does not detail normalization/scaling of xi before mapping to rotation angles, raising potential issues about angle domain suitability and sensitivity to raw price scale.

[inferred] Temporal data-splitting methodology: the dataset was randomly shuffled before train/validation/test splitting; for time series forecasting this can introduce information leakage and produce overly optimistic training dynamics.

[inferred] Lack of classical and ablation baselines: no direct comparisons to classical GAF, other encoding methods, or standard time-series models (e.g., LSTM, classical CNN on raw series) are reported, making it hard to attribute any effect to the quantum encoding.

[inferred] No economic/trading evaluation: results are reported in classification metrics only; there is no translation to trading performance, risk-adjusted returns, or incorporation of transaction costs.

key_ideas: #idea:hybrid-approach — Implemented a hybrid quantum-inspired feature engineering + classical CNN pipeline: map 20-day SMA and Bollinger Band windows into 20x20 QGAF images using single-qubit U3(theta,0,0) rotations in Qiskit Aer and classify next-day direction with a two-branch CNN.

#idea:hybrid-approach — QGAF encoding defined as Qi,j = cos(theta_i + theta_j) with theta_i = x_i (raw time-series value) produces quantum-inspired image representations intended for deep-learning classification.

#contradiction:classical-vs-quantum — Empirical results do not support a predictive advantage: test accuracy ~54.2% with severe overfitting (training >90%, validation ~50-55%) and a strong upward prediction bias, undermining claims that the quantum-inspired encoding improves forecasting.
#limitation:simulation-only — All quantum encoding steps were executed in a noise-free Qiskit AerSimulator (no real QPU experiments), limiting claims about practical quantum performance.
#limitation:qubit-count — The encoding uses a single qubit for the QGAF construction, raising questions about expressivity and scalability to richer quantum encodings for finance tasks.
#limitation:noise — Use of an idealized, noise-free simulator is identified as a limitation; outcomes may change under realistic noisy hardware conditions.
#limitation:data-encoding — Important preprocessing details (e.g., scaling of xi before mapping to rotation angle) are omitted, highlighting risks in the encoding choice and reproducibility.

#idea:hybrid-approach — The paper contributes a reproducible baseline description (frameworks, hyperparameters, data ranges) and diagnostics (confusion matrix, per-class metrics) useful for future comparisons and improvements.
contradictions: The reported empirical performance (54.2% test accuracy, severe overfitting and strong class bias) contradicts optimistic claims that quantum-inspired encodings like QGAF deliver clear predictive gains over classical feature engineering for stock-direction forecasting.

The study contradicts assertions of near-term scalability: the pipeline relies on a single-qubit, noise-free simulation and no hardware experiments, suggesting that positive results in simulation do not imply feasibility on noisy, larger-scale quantum hardware.
